text:
Lena: Quick follow-up after the MHA layout RFC review — we need to pick a pragmatic default for the runtime while we iterate on the longer refactor. My short summary: token-major (token, head, dim) gives better contiguous token access for short seqs and prefix caching; head-major (head, token, dim) is easier for head-wise kernels and when we do head-wise fused ops. Which do we pick as the default? Any strong objections to doing runtime autodetect and an adapter layer?

Sanjay: I prefer head-major for optimized head-wise kernels. Most of our optimized attention kernels (fused softmax + dropout, headwise matmul) assume head-major layout to keep the per-head GEMM contiguous. Head-major also halves the stride when we slice per-head. Downsides: cache behavior for short seq_len suffers a bit.

Amanda: Token-major helped in my microbench for chat-style traffic (seq_len 8-64). Observed ~12% lower token latency due to better prefetch locality when the KV cache is hot. I think we should measure on 1) small seq short sessions 2) long streaming sessions with KV. We should not bias only by kernel simplicity.

Jordan: Both valid. Can we auto-select based on workload profile? Example heuristics: if seq_len <= 128 and batch_size small -> token-major. If head_count >= 16 and we use headwise fused kernels -> head-major. Also consider KV cache layout: if we keep KV as token-major, we avoid a copy when appending tokens.

Sanjay: Auto-select is fine but watch out for ABI churn. We need stable inter-stage buffers so we don't recompile kernels frequently. Suggest an adapter layer: internal canonical layout (internal_layout) + thin converters at model load or when route changes. That keeps kernels simple and lets us pick best internal layout per-device.

Lena: Agreed on adapter layer. Two concrete proposals: 
1) Pick head-major as the canonical internal layout (easier for our current kernels), implement fast token-major <-> head-major in-place path for the small-seq case.
2) Use token-major internal by default and implement head-major exporters for heavy-head kernels.
Which is less engineering debt?

Amanda: Implementing very fast inplace transpose between layouts is non-trivial but doable. If we choose head-major internal then token-major paths must be extremely cheap (single memcpy + reshape for many shapes) or we lose the benefit. Conversely if token-major internal, many of our fused kernels require more complex strides. My vote: head-major internal + optimized convert for token-major hot path.

Jordan: A few low-level points we should not lose sight of: 
- Alignment: prefer 256B when doing multi-head fused kernels to satisfy vector load widths on Ampere+ and avoid TLB pressure.
- Packing: contiguous QKV (Q,K,V interleaved per token) simplifies prefetch when we stream tokens, but contiguous QKV hurts per-head GEMM since it interleaves heads.
- Stride vs packing: Strided head-major Q/K/V (separate tensors per Q/K/V) helps cuBLAS/cuDNN callers. Interleaved QKV helps NVTransformer-style fused kernels.

Sanjay: Perf numbers I ran quickly on A100: 
```
seq=16, heads=12, dim=64: head-major (separate Q/K/V): 1.00x baseline
seq=16, heads=12, dim=64: token-major (interleaved QKV): 0.88x latency (better)
seq=256, heads=24, dim=64: head-major (separate): 1.00x baseline
seq=256, heads=24, dim=64: token-major: 1.15x worse
```
These are rough but show the crossover at higher seq_len/head_count.

Amanda: Good to capture that. Also note KV cache memory growth: token-major KV where tokens are contiguous makes append cheap (just append block). For head-major KV you might need a reorganize when you snapshot or shard KV across GPUs. That impacts Dedicated/Private deployments where we shard across devices.

Lena: Operational constraints matter. For sharded workloads, head-major KV can improve network serialization if we shard by head. If we shard by token, token-major helps. So routing policy + sharding strategy ties into layout choice.

Jordan: Actionable path I propose: 
- Short-term (sprint): pick head-major as canonical internal layout because it minimizes kernel rework. Implement a fast converter path for token-major hot paths (seq_len <= 128). Add a runtime flag layout_hint and a scheduler hook to pick converter when route matches.
- Medium-term (quarter): refactor runtime buffers: introduce LayoutAdapter API at the runtime border so that model loaders and sharders can agree on a common wire format. This prevents ABI churn.
- Long-term: benchmark and build a small profiler that recommends layout per-route and persists that as a deployment policy.

Sanjay: +1. For the converter implement vectorized block transposes with tuned block sizes (B=32 or 64) and prefetch intrinsics. Make sure to test on quantized paths — int8 packed layouts might need different block sizes.

Amanda: I'll open a perf doc with more numbers and start a microbench harness for the converter. Please add cases for KV append, snapshot, and cross-device shard.

ci-bot: Build #3812: layout-adapter branch tests: unit=✅ integration=⚠️ (one flaky test: sharded-kv-append).

Lena: Thanks all — next steps: Amanda to own microbench (ETA 4d), Jordan to draft LayoutAdapter API RFC (ETA 1w), Sanjay to prototype converter kernel (ETA 2w). I'll update the original RFC with these follow-ups and link the perf doc. If no objections by EOD I'll land the head-major-as-internal decision for next sprint. :thumbsup:

Sanjay: No objections from me.

Amanda: Fine by me.

Jordan: Fine. Will start the RFC draft.
